newsitem.title: USA: Evergreen Media to buy Chancellor.
newsitem.headline: Evergreen Media to buy Chancellor.

text.p: Evergreen Media Corp said Tuesday it would buy Chancellor Broadcasting Co in a stock swap and then acquire 10 radio properties owned by Viacom Inc, creating a company worth about $5 billion.
Evergreen said it would swap 0.9091 share of its Class A common for each share of Chancellor, which closed Friday at 28-1/8.
Evergreen, whose own stock closed Friday at 32-3/4, said it would pay $1.075 billion cash for the 10 Viacom properties, located in Los Angeles, Chicago, New York, Washington and Detroit.
The combined Evergreen and Chancellor, to be called Chancellor Media Corp, will have 103 radio stations in 21 U.S. markets, with 1996 net revenues of more than $700 million, Evergreen said.

After the merger, which is expected to be tax-free, Evergreen shareholders will hold two-thirds of the combined companies' roughly 63 million common shares, while Chancellor shareholders will hold one-third, Evergreen said.
Chancellor Broadcasting Chairman Thomas Hicks will be chairman of Chancellor Media Corp.
Evergreen Chairman and Chief Executive Scott Ginsburg will be the new company's president and chief executive, and Evergreen Chief Financial Officer will be the new company's CFO.
The Evergreen-Chancellor merger agreement requires regulatory approval and approval by shareholders of both companies, Evergreen said.
